records.failure: A failed or unsupported organization capability must not become a finding, and must not disable the personal workflow or any unrelated tag.
records.name: Proprietary tag package
records.job: Define organization-specific tag workflows and policy extensions.
records.outcome: Apply a private policy with clear provenance and claim boundaries.
records.claim: A private extension capability, bounded so that a private policy can add obligations but never weaken a public claim.
records.method: An optional local registry separates tenant namespaces, credentials, policy revisions and permissions for each literal-policy job. Private rules cannot change public tag methods. A hosted organization service is planned.
records.inputs: A local operator authority, tenant credential, reviewed policy, private text file and a selection binding the exact job and revision. The practice example is invented.
records.outputs: A brief occurrence count, or optional permission-controlled private details for the selected tenant, job and revision. Local authority is checked; real organization ownership is not verified. A match is not a policy-violation verdict.
records.today: Use the local organization policy practice guide on Mac or Linux. Enroll separate tenants, grant limited permissions, select a reviewed job, pause or restore access, export privately and remove the registry. Nothing is uploaded. The hosted organization service is still planned.
supported: Available now — separate local tenant authority and per-job selections
Available now — limited credentials, revision binding, pause and revocation
Available now — permission-controlled exports and isolated literal-policy checks
Required before sale — agreed ownership, licensing and the actual customer scope
limits: Display names here are offering names, not adopted standard codes
A private policy must not dilute or misrepresent the public standard, and must never reuse a public tag code for a different claim
A private extension is not a private fork of the evidence standard; thresholds move one way only, upward
Underlying personal detection and evidence remain free
records.validation: The governed local registry passed 27 control groups and 73 actual command checks on both Mac and isolated Linux. A separate review accepted the original software boundaries. These results do not verify real organization identity, employee consent, commercial terms or independent accuracy.
records.privacy: A private policy must preserve consent and the public privacy commitments. Team payment does not waive no-telemetry (F-086) or capture boundaries (F-087) for the people whose content is checked.
records.release: The local software boundaries are accepted. Before a commercial service or sale, agree the actual customer scope, ownership and licensing, and complete the applicable consent, deployment and conformance checks. Future private policies each need their own validation.

PS.usageHTML:
Use this tag

Copy an AI answer, paste it and check. No account or install needed. Commands are checked, never run.

PS in Terminal

Prefer Terminal? Download the small PS-only source ZIP and unzip it. Open its folder, save an answer as response.txt, then run the command below on Linux or macOS with Python 3.12+. No packages, account or local service needed. Up to 20,000 characters. No redaction is performed.

Download PS source · PS download guide

python3 -I -S -B scripts/check-ps.py response.txt

Check on this device

Open aitrustid.com/#person/PS and choose Check on this device. Optional: save the public app for offline use and add it to your home screen. No answer is uploaded; the phone preview performs no redaction.

Developer local service (optional)

Developer preview: Linux, Python 3.12+ and an installed, working Podman engine. First setup downloads pinned dependencies. Read the full guide for private build-network options and the older manual Docker Compose path. This command does not install an engine; no Chrome Web Store release is offered.

Download source · Full setup guide

  1. Get the source

    Download and unzip the source, then open its folder. Or use Git:

    git clone https://github.com/knwvmbrr/aitrust-id.git
cd aitrust-id

  2. Start your own checker

    On Linux with Python 3.12+ and a working Podman engine, run this from the source folder. It creates a private installation and checks that it works:

    python3 scripts/setup-local.py --engine podman

  3. Check an answer

    Save an answer as response.txt, then run:

    LOCAL_STATE="$HOME/.config/aitrust-id/local-stack"
"$LOCAL_STATE/checker/bin/python" scripts/aitrust.py check response.txt --env-file "$LOCAL_STATE/runtime.env"

A PS finding asks you to review a command pattern. No finding means no supported pattern was found, not “safe.” If a check cannot finish, it says so.

Optional Chrome tags: follow docs/gateway-authentication.md in the downloaded repository to set up gateway signing. Open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode, choose Load unpacked and select the extension folder. In its settings, choose your gateway public-key JSON, confirm its fingerprint separately and enter your local token. Turn on Enable checks on ChatGPT when ready. Keep your services running. Tags appear below supported answers; click for a short explanation. Unsigned or altered results stay unavailable. Pause or reset at any time.

Your answer goes to your own local service, not this website or a training database. Keep your token private. Do not paste it into a public report.

Repeat a saved local-service check. This compares your saved findings against the same method; it does not send research data to us.

Stop the checker

python3 scripts/setup-local.py --engine podman --stop
